{{Short description|French probability theorist}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=August 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=August 2021}}
'''Florence Merlevède''' is a French [[probability theory|probability theorist]] whose research interests focus on [[Independence (probability theory)|dependent]] and [[weakly dependent random variables]], including [[Bernstein inequalities (probability theory)|Bernstein inequalities]] and [[central limit theorem]]s for these variables. She is a professor in the laboratory for analysis and applied mathematics at [[Gustave Eiffel University]], associated with the research group on probability and statistics there.{{r|lama}}

Merlevède earned her Ph.D. at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in 1996, with a dissertation jointly supervised by Denis Bosq and [[Magda Peligrad]].{{r|mg}} With Peligrad and Sergey Utev, she is coauthor of the book ''Functional Gaussian Approximation for Dependent Structures'' (Oxford University Press, 2019).{{r|fga}} She is on the editorial board of the journal ''[[Probability Theory and Related Fields]]''.<ref>{{cite web
| title = Probability Theory and Related Fields editors
| url = https://link.springer.com/journal/440/editors
| access-date = 15 March 2024
| url-status = live
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20240315093717/https://link.springer.com/journal/440/editors
| archive-date = 15 March 2024}}</ref>

In 2021, Merlevède was named a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], "for outstanding contributions to the field of dependent random variables, especially for fundamental results concerning the conditional limit theorems, rates of convergence in the central limit theorem, and large random matrices".{{r|fims}}
